title: Detroit Institute of Arts: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works that make the relationship between a figure and its surroundings impossible to ignore.
introduction:
A worker in Rivera's factory has a task and a place within a vast system. The sleeper in Fuseli's *The Nightmare* occupies an equally definite space, but the beings around her make its rules uncertain. Between these extremes, a bar, a study and a bookshop show people giving shape to their everyday surroundings.

This selection from the Detroit Institute of Arts follows those different kinds of enclosure. A room can protect concentration, organise labour or trap a body. It can also be opened up by colour until its walls cease to feel solid. The works do not offer a common answer; they provide useful ways of asking how much space a person has, and who or what controls it.
visitNote: Check current gallery information for display changes and loans. The Rivera entry represents the north wall of the Detroit Industry murals, not the complete cycle. Attribution and dating follow the cited object evidence; the two Saint Jerome panels have different authorship histories.

books.title: The Practice and Science of Drawing
books.author: Harold Speed
books.note: Speed’s discussion of mass, line and tone offers a way into both small panels and large figure groups. Compare the tightly outlined bodies in Rivera with the nearly dissolved forms in Whistler.

works.title: The Nightmare
works.credit: Henry Fuseli. The Nightmare. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The sleeper's body lies across the bed while a creature sits squarely on her torso. Behind them, a horse's head enters through the dark curtains. Fuseli gives these intruders the same physical presence as the furniture. A nightmare is represented as an occupation of the room: the woman cannot respond, while the impossible beings appear entirely at home.

works.title: Detroit Industry: North Wall
works.credit: Diego Rivera. Detroit Industry, North Wall. Image: WikiArt. Copyright protected (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Repeated bodies and pipes carry activity across Rivera's factory scene. Each worker has a local task, yet the mural's scale insists on the larger system joining those tasks together. Made in 1932–1933, the North Wall belongs to a surrounding fresco cycle. A reproduction can clarify individual actions, but it cannot reproduce the experience of industrial production occupying an entire architectural enclosure.

works.title: Nocturne in Black and Gold: The Falling Rocket
works.catalogueTitle: Nocturne in Black and Gold – the Falling Rocket
works.credit: James Abbott McNeill Whistler. Nocturne in Black and Gold – the Falling Rocket. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Gold marks descend through darkness without describing every stage of the firework's path. Water, figures and distance remain only partially resolved. Whistler gives enough information to recognise a spectacle, then leaves colour and scattered light to do the rest. The lack of detail is functional: a fully mapped setting would compete with the brief visibility of the falling sparks.

works.title: Martha and Mary Magdalene
works.credit: Martha and Mary Magdalene. WikiArt; Caravaggio. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The mirror makes appearance an object within the conversation. One woman speaks; the other's hand turns attention towards her own body. Caravaggio brings the religious subject into this close exchange, withholding a larger public setting. The changing relation between the women matters more than spectacle: a gesture can register a response that an elaborately described room would not explain.

works.title: The Window
works.credit: Henri Matisse. The Window. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/henri-matisse/the-window-1916
works.description: Matisse places the green outside beside the blue interior with a firmness that can make distance seem almost optional. Table, chair and flowers remain recognisable, but their outlines also divide the canvas into neighbouring areas. The window therefore works in two ways: as an opening in a room and as a boundary between colours on a flat surface.

works.title: Cotopaxi
works.credit: Frederic Edwin Church. Cotopaxi (Ecuador). Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Smoke spreads beyond the volcano until the eruption changes the light of the whole view. Church combines a carefully articulated foreground with a horizon that cannot remain stable. The landscape's small details provide a scale against which the event can be measured. The important action is not confined to the mountain; it is carried through the reddish air.

works.title: Saint Jerome in His Study
works.medium: Oil on linen paper on oak panel
works.credit: Jan van Eyck. St. Jerome in his Study. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/jan-van-eyck/st-jerome-in-his-study-1432
works.description: Books and instruments make Jerome's study a place of disciplined attention. The lion at his feet brings the saint's legend into that intellectual setting. This is a very small panel, about twenty centimetres high, whose objects reward close inspection. Its attribution has varied historically; the DIA currently lists Jan van Eyck and a date of about 1435.

works.title: Saint Jerome in the Desert
works.artist: Workshop of Rogier van der Weyden
works.credit: Saint Jerome and the Lion. WikiArt; Rogier van der Weyden. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Here Jerome attends to the lion's paw rather than to the books surrounding him in the previous work. Angular rocks enclose the pair, giving an outdoor episode the concentration of a small room. The museum attributes the panel to Rogier van der Weyden's workshop, a distinction worth preserving: its connection to a master's practice does not establish that he painted it himself.

works.title: McSorley's Bar
works.credit: John Sloan. McSorley's Bar. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Leaning, standing and waiting give Sloan's bar its social arrangement. The white-clad worker draws attention within the dark room, but no incident makes everyone else a supporting character. Pictures and fixtures crowd the walls as the men occupy the counter. This is a space understood through repeated use, where the distribution of bodies matters more than an identifiable story.

works.title: Love Flight of a Pink Candy Heart
works.catalogueTitle: Love Flight of a Pink Candy Heart
works.credit: Florine Stettheimer. Love Flight of a Pink Candy Heart. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Stettheimer does not ask every figure and ornament to obey a common scale. Small people, bright signs and the pink heart-like form share a yellow field according to their pictorial importance rather than their physical size. The result can be read through its scattered incidents, without forcing them into the continuous space expected of a conventional scene.

works.title: Bookshop: Hebrew Books, Holy Day Books
works.catalogueTitle: Bookshop: Hebrew Books, Holy Day Books
works.credit: Ben Shahn. Bookshop: Hebrew Books, Holy Day Books. Image: WikiArt. Copyright protected (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The lettering tells us what kind of shop this is before the figure at its door can tell us anything about a particular day. Shahn lets words carry cultural information that a generic storefront would lose. Thin lines hold doorway, sign and person together. The red entrance gives that precise, modest business a place within the street.

works.title: Study for Crouching Nude
works.credit: Francis Bacon. Study for Crouching Nude. WikiArt source label: Francis Bacon Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/francis-bacon/study-for-crouching-nude-1952
works.license: Francis Bacon Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Bacon surrounds the crouching body with a cage-like diagram, then refuses to give the anatomy an equally settled shape. The contrast matters: the enclosure offers clear boundaries against which the figure's instability becomes apparent. Vertical streaks disturb the darkness behind it. Confinement is carried by the body's position and by the measured structure that leaves it so little room.

works.title: View of the Outskirts of Paris
works.catalogueTitle: View of the Outskirts of Paris
works.credit: Henri Rousseau. View of the Outskirts of Paris. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/henri-rousseau/view-of-the-outskirts-of-paris-1896
works.description: Rousseau's factories and chimneys stand as clear, separated shapes beyond the river. Industry enters the landscape without the crowded activity of Rivera's mural. The difference is one of viewpoint as much as subject: this observer remains outside, on a bank from which production appears as buildings rather than labour. The quiet arrangement does not tell us what happens inside them.

works.title: The Appeal (Two Women and a Man)
works.catalogueTitle: The Appeal (Two Women and a Man)
works.credit: Two women and a man ( Trio). WikiArt; Giorgione. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Hands and glances link the three closely grouped figures, but their relationship does not yield an unambiguous story. The work has also received changing attributions and titles. The DIA now catalogues it as Titian's *The Appeal*, dated to the early–mid sixteenth century. An attentive reading can follow the exchange without pretending that either the scene or its authorship has always been settled.

works.title: The Holy Family
works.credit: Nicolas Poussin. The Holy Family. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Mary bends towards the child and cradle while Joseph occupies a more distant place. Poussin gives these unequal degrees of closeness a firm architectural setting. Drapery and the tall opening hold the room together without obscuring the small act of care at its centre. The sacred subject rests on a recognisable division between attending directly and remaining nearby.

works.title: The Blind Leading the Blind
works.credit: Louise Bourgeois. The Blind Leading the Blind. Image: WikiArt. Copyright protected (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Bourgeois connects the pink uprights with a shared horizontal bar, but their tapering lower ends make that collective structure look precarious. The title suggests a group of people without requiring heads or complete bodies. Support and dependence can be examined in the construction itself: each repeated element belongs to the whole, yet the whole offers no comfortably broad footing.

works.title: The Elbe near Dresden
works.credit: Oskar Kokoschka. The Elbe Near Dresden. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The church tower and town retain their identities amid Kokoschka's strongly worked colour. Blue water and red and green bands give the banks an activity that continues into the sky. Rather than placing fixed buildings before a changing river, the painting subjects the whole view to an unsettled surface. Architecture participates in the movement instead of stopping it.

works.title: The Wolf River, Kansas
works.credit: Albert Bierstadt. The Wolf River, Kansas. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Tents and people occupy a clearing beneath tall trees. Bierstadt's distant vantage makes their activities part of a much larger distribution of light and shade. It is useful to notice the limits of that vantage: the painting shows an inhabited place, but its small figures do not provide a full account of the people who live there.

works.title: Girl with a Mandolin
works.credit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo. Girl with a Mandolin. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The instrument gives the woman's hands a shared task and carries a diagonal across her body. Her turning head prevents the pose from becoming an evenly presented display of costume. Tiepolo brings pale skin and bright fabric out of the dark setting, but the painting's animation depends on that slight mismatch between the direction of the face and the occupied hands.

works.title: Job
works.credit: Job. WikiArt; WikiArt. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; complete source frame.
works.description: Jordaens makes the weathered face and exposed chest the substance of Job's appeal. The upward gaze carries the biblical subject without dissolving the man into an abstract emblem of patience. Light crosses flesh that appears vulnerable and particular. After the factories, landscapes and rooms in this selection, a body and a lifted pair of eyes are enough.

closingSections.title: Return to the scale of a body
paragraphs: Compare Rivera's workers with Bacon's enclosed figure, then with the reader in the small Van Eyck panel. The different settings give a body different freedoms. These are collection selections, not a guaranteed display route; check current museum records when planning a visit, especially for works with changing attributions or exhibition status.
